title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is printed upside down. It is page '- 19 -' of a French typescript on cohomology in sites and topoi. It has been filed within cote 14 (algebraic cycles, Hodge/Tate/Lefschetz/Weil). The neighbouring pages are handwritten notes on algebraic cycles on abelian varieties, unrelated to this one.

Content:
(i) The end of a proof. Let R be the sieve generated by a covering family (U_i -> X). The sheaf associated to R is isomorphic to the sheaf associated to X. Applying the preceding proposition and formula (19) gives the Cartan–Leray spectral sequence of a covering, E_2^{pq} = \check H^p((U_i), H^q(F)) => H^{p+q}(X,F). A handwritten correction changes 'due à' to 'celle de' Cartan–Leray.
(ii) Corollary 2.5. Passing to the inductive limit over coverings gives a spectral sequence, functorial in F and in X: \check H^p(X, \mathcal H^q(F)) => H^{p+q}(C^~/X, F). Here \mathcal H^q(F) is the presheaf U |-> H^q(U,F). Letting X vary gives a spectral sequence of presheaves \check{\mathcal H}^p(\mathcal H^q(F)) => \mathcal H^{p+q}(F).
(iii) The edge maps Φ^q: \check{\mathcal H}^q(\mathcal H^0 F) -> \mathcal H^q(F) and Φ^q_X: \check H^q(X, \mathcal H^0 F) -> H^q(X,F) are isomorphisms for q = 0, 1 and monomorphisms for q = 2. More generally, if the presheaves \mathcal H^i(F) vanish for 0 < i < n, they are isomorphisms for q ≤ n and monomorphisms for q = n+1.
(iv) The proof begins: take the inductive limit of the spectral sequence of Proposition 2.3 ...

This is the standard comparison of Čech cohomology with derived-functor cohomology on a site, as in SGA 4 Exposé V (Verdier), §2–3. It belongs to the foundations of étale cohomology, not to the cycle conjectures.
errors: No mathematical errors. The standard facts used are that \check H^0 of the presheaf \mathcal H^q(F) vanishes for q > 0, which yields iso for q ≤ 1 and mono for q = 2, and the analogous connectivity argument for the general n. Both are correct.
Archival note: the typescript page is misfiled inside the cycles dossier and is scanned upside down.
